title: Repository Governance
purpose: Own repository-wide authority, vocabulary, evidence precedence, placement law, rule assurance, and governance lifecycle without absorbing domain specifications.

constructs.name: principle
constructs.meaning: Stable repository-wide invariant that constrains subordinate policy and rules.

constructs.name: policy
constructs.meaning: Authoritative decision framework that governs a defined scope.

constructs.name: rule
constructs.meaning: Testable mandatory statement with a stable identity and assurance contract.

constructs.name: requirement
constructs.meaning: Domain-scoped mandatory statement governed by its specification owner and assurance contract.

constructs.name: implementation
constructs.meaning: Executable mechanism that makes a prescription true.

constructs.name: verification
constructs.meaning: Executable or bounded check that evaluates a prescription against state.

constructs.name: evidence
constructs.meaning: Revision-bound result emitted by verification or an accepted evidence source.

constructs.name: projection
constructs.meaning: Derived human or machine view that cannot write back authority.

normative_authority.rule: Only the registered canonical owner may define or change a governed normative fact. Non-owning sources may reference or project it but cannot override it.

examples: declared implementation status in specification metadata

evidence_model.conflict_rule: For observed implementation state, fresher evidence in a higher-precedence conformance class wins. A lower-precedence source MUST NOT override a conflicting higher-precedence observation. Normative ownership is resolved separately through the canonical owner registry.
evidence_model.freshness_rule: Evidence without resolvable evaluated revision or input provenance is stale for conformance claims.

validation_policy.review_policy: Human review MUST be used only when deterministic or bounded machine validation is infeasible or disproportionate for the residual question.

rules.statement: Every persistent governed artefact MUST resolve to exactly one primary semantic role.
Every prescriptive artefact and governed fact MUST resolve to exactly one canonical authoritative owner.
Every persistent governed artefact MUST resolve to exactly one legal Directory Grammar slot.
Unknown persistent governed top-level directories, governed subdirectories, and artefact classes MUST fail closed.
Generated outputs MUST remain projection-only and MUST NOT become write-back or normative authority.
Every deterministic governed rule MUST name a unique failing fixture that demonstrates detection of its prohibited state.
Every new persistent grammar slot MUST cite a concrete issue or governed change that demonstrates the need before the slot can become active.

residual_review.justification: Mechanical validation can prove the source exists and is typed, but only bounded governance review can judge whether the cited need is substantively justified.
residual_review.bounded_question: Does the cited issue/change demonstrate a current persistent structural need rather than speculative hierarchy?

rules.statement: .work MUST remain the reserved disposable KIS change/work namespace and MUST NOT become canonical product authority, published content, or required product input.
Human review MUST NOT be the primary validation method when deterministic or bounded machine validation is feasible.
Repository-wide Governance and the MRD Specification MUST have distinct canonical domains and MUST NOT own each other's normative concerns.
Conformance claims MUST follow the governed evidence precedence and MUST reject stale or lower-precedence evidence that conflicts with fresher higher-precedence evidence.
The enforcement register MUST be a deterministic non-authoritative projection of canonical governed rules and MUST NOT be independently authored.
Every registered prescriptive artefact MUST have a deterministic human projection route or an explicit governed non-publication reason.
MRD stable identity MUST be opaque to classification and location, while classification, canonical path, lifecycle, exact Git revision, and GitHub change provenance remain separate metadata.
Every mandatory Repository Governance rule MUST resolve its implementation, validator, execution point, failure code, and evidence location to concrete repository artefacts.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: Every registered repository relationship MUST use a governed relationship contract with a legal direction, target role, target slot, and slot capability.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: A non-owning prescriptive artefact MUST NOT independently restate a canonical repository-wide governed rule as normative authority.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

residual_review.justification: Mechanical validation detects rule-ID reuse and normalized exact restatement; bounded semantic review is required only for materially equivalent paraphrases that cannot be decided reliably by deterministic text matching.
residual_review.bounded_question: Does a changed non-owning prescriptive artefact create a second normative statement materially equivalent to a canonical Repository Governance rule?

rules.statement: Governed vocabulary relationships and rule lifecycle transitions MUST use the canonical vocabulary and resolve supersession references without self-reference or dangling targets.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: Every canonical governed rule MUST conform to the governed-rule schema, including stable identity, rationale origin, scope, ownership, implementation, verification, evidence, and lifecycle fields.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: High-risk authority artefact classes MUST be explicitly prohibited from generated, verification, evidence, implementation, and change-record slots in addition to positive allow-list enforcement.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: Every active Directory Grammar slot MUST contain the complete governed slot contract: purpose, permitted and prohibited types, roles, authority constraints, relationships, editability, generation status, lifecycle, retention, verification, and origin.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: Every governed rule MUST state its applicability scope and MUST cite the defect, obligation, or governed change that explains why the rule exists.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

rules.statement: Residual human review MUST be explicitly justified, capability-bounded, question-bounded, evidence-located, and result-contracted after deterministic validation has done all feasible work.

applies_to: repository governance model and governed repository state

operator_governance_policy.heading: kis-op Governance Behavior
operator_governance_policy.purpose: Prescribe how kis-op applies the governance model when inspecting, planning, changing, validating, and presenting governed repository work.

phases.name: resolve_authority
required_actions: load repository authority and active change scope
identify canonical owners relevant to the request

phases.name: select_applicable_mrds
required_actions: select the minimum sufficient MRD set
stop_when: a required need has no representable type and no governed extension path

phases.name: resolve_relationships
required_actions: detect duplicate ownership and authority conflicts
stop_when: required dependency or canonical owner is unresolved

phases.name: validate_governance
required_actions: run structural and semantic governance validation
surface stable reason codes for blocking failures

phases.name: execute_bounded_change
required_actions: work only inside the admitted change scope
preserve parent KIS trust and Git authority
avoid unrelated documentation or platform expansion
stop_when: requested mutation exceeds admitted scope or authority

phases.name: generate_review_surface
required_actions: generate the HRD specification from validated MRDs
preserve provenance and deterministic source bindings
stop_when: source validation or deterministic generation fails

phases.name: verify_and_report
required_actions: verify generated output is current and untampered
report completion, gaps, deferrals, and diagnostics against the requested scope

outputs: applicability decision or identified MRD set
